public_rationale: The claim has two parts. The user-growth part holds for Q1 2026: The Information, as reported by Digital Today, said ChatGPT averaged about 905 million weekly users in the quarter and could not climb past the 920 million it passed in late February. The conversion part is weaker. OpenAI's own figures imply only about 5.6% of weekly users pay, which is a small share. But OpenAI said subscriber momentum 'accelerated meaningfully,' with January and February on track to be its biggest months ever for new subscribers. That cuts against 'continues to struggle' as a trend. So the stall part is supported and the conversion part is not clearly borne out. Growth resumed later: ChatGPT passed 1 billion weekly users in July 2026.
limitations: User figures come from a secondhand report of The Information, not primary data.
Subscriber momentum is OpenAI's own characterisation.
'Struggle' has no threshold, so the reading drives the result.
